rules.name: Initiative Training
rules.description: If an infantry NCO is killed, roll a D6. On 1 the NCO is killed as normal, on 2-6 one of the other members takes over the squad and leads as effectively as before. If the NCO is successfully replaced the unit does not suffer the usual -1 morale penalty for losing its NCO.

rules.name: Hitler's Buzzsaw
rules.description: German units equipped with LMGs and MMGs fire one extra shot (5 for a LMG and 6 for a MMG).

rules.name: Blitzkrieg
rules.description: German officers using the ‘You men, snap to action’ special rule can take one additional order die from the bag and assign it as normal.

rules.name: Tiger Fear
rules.description: All enemy units that are within 18” of, and have line of sight to, one or more vehicle with the Tiger Fear special rule suffer from Tiger Fear, the unit count as having one extra pin marker on them when taking any order test except if ordered to Fire against a vehicle causing Tiger fear. Note that the 18” range is measured AFTER you have declared which order you have given to the unit.

rules.name: Early Grenadier
rules.description: Units of Heer Grenadiers and Heer Veteran Grenadiers cannot be equipped with assault rifles.

rules.name: Early Panther
rules.description:
Rushed into combat for Operation Citadel, the Panther had many technical and mechanical problems. If chosen from this list, the Panther must roll a D6 each time it completes a move. On a 2+ it is it fine. On a 1 there is a problem, roll again. To compensate for this, the requisition points cost of these Panthers is reduced by 10 percent, rounding up to the next whole number (e.g. a vehicle that normally costs 390pts would instead cost 351pts).
1 Abandoned. The Panther breaks down and crew abandon it, running for the rear. It counts as destroyed. 2–3 Breakdown. The Panther breaks down and is immobilised at the end of its move. It may still Fire 4+ The Panther is stalled, but the crew will get it running again. It cannot move next turn. After missing a turn it can start moving again.

rules.name: Defences
rules.description:
As well as pillboxes and bunkers, a resistance nest should also be well supplied with trenches, sandbagged dug-outs, barbed wire and other obstacles. If the force is the defender, each platoon taken from this selector gets the following advantages:
• The platoon receives either one bunker or two hard cover linear obstacles.
• Each linear obstacle must be up to 6" long and 1" tall, and should provide hard cover (so use low walls, earth embankments, sandbags and the like). You can replace any number of hard cover linear obstacles with soft cover ones (barbed wire, hedges, picket fences, etc.); if you do so, you get two soft cover obstacles for each hard cover one you surrender. Bunkers should be large enough to accommodate a single unit of infantry or artillery. The rules for bunkers are on page 127 of the Bolt Action rulebook.

rules.name: Fuel Shortages
rules.description:
By now the supply situation was critical and the German Army could no longer easily keep its big vehicles running. Roll a D6 for any of the above vehicles marked * after completing a move. To compensate for this, the requisition points cost of each of these vehicles is reduced by 10 percent, rounding up (e.g. a vehicle that normally costs 137pts would instead cost 123.3pts, rounded up to 124pts).
1 Out of fuel. The vehicle completes its move and is then immobilised. It cannot move for the rest of the game, but may continue to Fire. 2 Fuel low. The vehicle may make one more move after this one, then runs out of fuel as above. 3+ Fuel OK. The vehicle still has enough fuel to move normally.

rules.name: Until Extinction
rules.description: The Blue Division’s motto was “Sin relevo posible, hasta la extinción“ (English: No possible relief, until Extinction), they were very stubborn fighters, at Krasny Bor surrounded Spaniards fought to the death. All Spanish infantry and artillery units can be upgraded to Fanatics at the cost of +2 points per man.

rules.name: “Spaniards die on their feet, not hiding in holes like rats”
rules.description: The Spaniards were reluctant to “waste” time digging or maintaining trenches, they also often walked around in the open within range of Soviet snipers. To reflect their contempt for cover, the enemy never suffer more than a -1 modifier to their roll to hit when firing at Spanish troops in cover, even if the targets are in hard cover.

rules.name: Forward the Guns
rules.description: Forward the Guns:German anti-tank units were highly aggressive. The player may reroll failed order tests for his anti-tank guns (artillery units only) when testing for an Advance or Run order. This also includes anti-tank guns being towed and moved into position.

rules.name: Desert Fighters
rules.description: Desert Fighters: (Due to the inclusion of ethnic Arab and former Foreign Legion personnel in the 90th, they get the Desert Fighters trait.)

rules.name: Motorized Infantry
rules.description: The platoon must include enough transport vehicles to transport all infantry and artillery units.

sharedRules.name: Volks Grenadiers
sharedRules.description: Volksgrenadiers are Green: if updated to Regular roll again, on a further roll of 5 or 6 they are immediately uprated again to Veterans.

sharedRules.name: Paranoia
sharedRules.description: When the enemy rolls on the Fubar chart, they suffer a -2 modifier to the roll, such is the paranoia induced in the enemy by this squads irregular activities.

sharedRules.name: Sabotage!
sharedRules.description: Enemy units in Reserve suffer an additional -1 modifier on the test to come on to the table. In addition, outflanking enemy units must take another test when they become available (still with an additional -1 modifier), and if they fail it, they can only be deployed up to 12" from their table edge along the chosen short table edge.

sharedRules.name: Italian MMG
sharedRules.description: This tank does not benefit from Hitler's Buzzsaw special rule.

sharedRules.name: Motorised infantry
sharedRules.description: The squad can re-roll any failed order test that is required to mount or dismount a transport vehicle.

sharedRules.name: Mobile Fortress
sharedRules.description: To fulfil its role as a breakthrough tank the Maus had extremely heavy armour. There is no penetration modifier for hitting a Maus from the side and the penetration modifier for hitting a Maus in its rear arc is reduced to +1.

sharedRules.name: Co Axial Main Gun
sharedRules.description: Although the Co-axially mounted 75mm KWK44 L36 would in any other tank be a respectable anti-tank gun, it was fitted on the Maus to provide dedicated HE fire. For the purposes of these rules it is classed as a Light Howitzer.

sharedRules.name: Fuel Shortage
sharedRules.description: By now the supply situation was critical and the German Army could no longer easily keep its big vehicles running. Roll a D6 for any of the above vehicles marked after completing a move. To compensate for this, the requisition points cost of each of these vehicles is reduced by 10 percent, rounding up (e.g. a vehicle that normally costs 137pts would instead cost 123.3pts, rounded up to 124pts).

sharedRules.name: Maus in Bolt Action
sharedRules.description: Whilst the Maus may not have entered combat during WW2 there is no reason why you cannot field this mighty vehicle in your games of Bolt Action. Of course any operational Maus prototype would have fought during the dying days of the Third Reich.

sharedRules.name: 200mm Infrared Searchlight
sharedRules.description: The infrared searchlight confers a +24" modifier to the Panther's spotting rolls.

sharedRules.name: Coaxial cannon
sharedRules.description: Tanks with two coaxial heavy weapons in a single turret may only fire one weapon per turn

sharedRules.name: Panzerbüchse
sharedRules.description: Counts as a light anti-tank gun, and in addition its squeeze-bore system means that ranges of up to 12", its base armour penetration is increased by two to a total of +6, at over half range armour penetration is reduced by two instead of the usual one to a total of +2.

sharedRules.name: Assault gun riders
sharedRules.description: An assault gun rider unit can mount or dismount from an assault gun or tankdestroy er counting it as a transport for these purposes. Once dismounted the unit is replaced bya few assault gun rider models placed on the assault gun itself. One unit of assault gun riderscan ride upon one assault gun or tank destroy er. As with other transported units the assault gun riders cannot be targeted whilst they ride upon their assault gun; however, unlike with other troops, assault gun riders must immediately disembark if the assault gun they are riding upon is shot at. Regardless of what kind of weapon is shooting at the assault gun, as long as the firer is within range of the assault gun the assault gun riders disembark when the shot is declared and before rolling the dice to determine hits. Units disembarking in this way immediately go ‘down’ or remain ‘down’ if they are down already.

sharedRules.name: Luftfaust
sharedRules.description: The Luftfaust counts as a light autocannon that only fires HE rounds and has a range of 24” instead of 48”. It does not have the Team and Fixed special rules, but instead it has the Flak and One-Shot special rules.

sharedRules.name: Götterdämmerung
sharedRules.description: Roll a die every time the vehicle completes a move: 1:Broken down/out of fuel: The vehicle is immobilised for the rest of the game. 2 Breaking down/fuel low: The vehicle may make one more move after this one, then runs out of fuel and is immobilised. 3+: OK: Continue as normal, rolling again after next move.

sharedRules.name: Gewehr 43
sharedRules.description: The team does not suffer the -1 penality for advancing and shooting, also after resolving shooting roll a die, on a result of 4+ a Veteran sniper gets a second shot. On a roll of 5+ a Regular sniper gets a second shot. This second shot is taken at the same target.

sharedRules.name: Conflicting Loyalties
sharedRules.description:
This unit counts as Green. However, when rolling after the first casualty, use the following table instead:
1-3: This unit immediately goes Down and gains the Shirkers rule for the rest of the game.
4-6: The unit immediately becomes Regular and Stubborn for the rest of the game.

rules.name: Stielgranate 41
rules.description: Can be used from 1942 onwards. Weapons penetration +2, but only at short range.

rules.name: Versatile
rules.description: This weapon can also be fired as a light howitzer.

rules.name: Remote-operated mine
rules.description:
The Goliath Model itself is just a marker, and it is treated as a one-shot weapon with a range of 18". Goliaths can only target stationary targets, either a stationary vehicle (i.e. any vehicle that is not sporting an order dice showing a Run or Advance order) or a unit inside a building. Goliaths are fired as normal, except instead of rolling to hit, roll on the following chart. Note that if a Recce vehicle reacts to the Goliath attack my moving, the mine automatically scores a result of 1-4.

Dice	Effect
1-4	The Goliath breaks down, or is damaged or prematurely detonated by	enemy fire. The Goliath model is removed and has no effect. 

5-6	The Goliath reaches the target and is detonated. If the target is a vehicle, it suffers a hit with a Pen of +7 (no Pen modifiers apply). If the target is a unit inside a building, the unit is hit by the equivalent of a heavy howitzer - remember that if this explosion scores 12 or more hits, it brings down the entire building, killing everyone inside!

rules.name: Intelligence
rules.description: Once per game, at the beginning of any turn before the first die is drawn from the dice bag. Roll a D6 and apply modifiers: Inexperienced -1, Veteran +1. On a 4+, the player activating the Intelligence Officer may choose a die from the bag for the first activation. If both players attempt to activate this ability simultaneously, each must roll 1D6. The higher score wins and immediately uses this ability, but the losing player may attempt to use his ability on another turn instead.

rules.name: Inspiring Presence
rules.description: Upon receiving his order dice (except for Down), a chaplain may select one friendly unit within 6" and roll a D6, applying the following modifiers: Inexperienced -1, Veteran +1. On a 4+, the chaplain may remove 1 pin from the selected unit.

rules.name: Non Combatant
rules.description: The chaplain is there to support the soldiers, not win battles. A chaplain unit cannot be used to claim or contest objectives.

rules.name: Self-defence only
rules.description: Clergymen are not soldiers and will not take part in hostile actions - they cannot fire any weapon, nor assault enemy units. If your chaplain is equipped with a pistol, it can only be used in close quarters if the enemy assaults him (including firing it at the assaulting enemies as a reaction, if applicable).

rules.name: Gun assembly
rules.description: To simulate the fact that the gun was actually transported disassembled, when the gun is unlimbered the artillery unit suffers a pin. When the gun is limbered, the mule team (and consequently the transported artillery unit) suffers a pin.

rules.name: Stubborn (Mule)
rules.description: When taking an order test and doubles are rolled, the mules become stubborn and refuse to cooperate even if the order test was passed. Place the order dice to Down and add 1 pin marker to th eteam. This rule does not apply if Fubar is rolled.
